prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Scope: hospital automated medication dispensing/returns: order intake, pharmacy prep/verification, cold storage, tube transport, ward cabinets, returns. Goals: timeliness, oversight, traceability. Aliases: Morrowglass=Medication Order Gateway; Cinderwake=Pharmacy Fulfillment Robot; Juniper=Pharmacy Verification Station; Bluejay=Sensor-monitored Medication Cooler; Tallowmere=Medication Return Kiosk; Copperfield=Pharmacy Technician; Larkspur=Registered Nurse; Stonewake=Biomedical Engineer. Elements: - Medication Order Gateway: validates orders, flags bad data, routes to pharmacy, sends order status, produces Order Reconciliation Snapshot. - Pharmacy Verification Station: final check, records outcome, blocks incomplete release, produces Batch Release Note, audit record. - Pharmacy Fulfillment Robot: prepares authorized orders only, presents package at Station, produces Priority Refill Tote Tag. - Sensor-monitored Medication Cooler: records temperature, displays current temperature/excursions, reports excursion/connectivity loss. - Pneumatic Tube Network: accepts only compliant loads. - East/West Tube Dispatch Consoles: route deliveries; East checks route availability, monitors capsules, records route/timing/status, sends Tube Route Exception Ticket. - North/South Ward Cabinet Controllers: report availability, block dispensing when Out of Service, record arrival time/destination cabinet for own ward; North uses Priority Refill Tote Tag to confirm ward before tote acceptance. - Medication Return Kiosk: guides return-bin checks, records outcomes, produces Return Bin Audit Label. Actors: - Clinical Pharmacist: exceptions, stock judgments, Dose Exception Review Slip. - Pharmacy Technician: prep, content checks, Cold Chain Handoff Card, capsule checks, uses Return Bin Audit Label for collection. - Hospital Courier: handoff checks, Pneumatic Capsule Seal Record, manual transport. - Medication Safety Officer: Diversion Review Packet. - Charge Nurse: Cabinet Downtime Notice. - Registered Nurse: confirms need, verifies load intended for ward, checks refrigerated handling, confirms return eligibility/separation. - Biomedical Engineer, IT Operations Specialist: repair. - Dispatch, Operations staff. Modes: route Faulted/Available; cabinet Out of Service/Ready for Dispense. Rules: discrepancies block prep; release after checks; capsule identifiers/destination reconciled before admission; route/packaging problem holds load until resolved/documented; automation unavailable -> staff custody, approved alternate delivery; receiver confirms arrival, reports discrepancies; ward receipt check (packaging, identifiers legible vs task list, quantity/descriptions); mismatched

New part:
S118: Staff reconcile the bin contents with the return entry before the bin is closed.
S119: Questionable or damaged returned medication is segregated and referred for review rather than combined with accepted returns.
S120: A checked return bin remains secured in its designated holding location until collection is authorized.
S121: The Hospital Courier collects only bins that are closed and recorded as ready for collection.
S122: The Charge Nurse ensures that unresolved receipt or return discrepancies remain assigned for follow-up at shift handover.
S123: A dose exception is any mismatch, omission, duplicate request, or clinically implausible value detected before a medication is released for use.
S124: The affected transaction remains on hold until an authorized reviewer documents a disposition.
S125: The Pharmacy Fulfillment Robot stops the affected pick sequence and keeps the package in a controlled hold location pending review.
S126: Cinderwake preserves the scanned product and quantity data associated with the exception.
S127: Juniper compares the active order with the scanned product, strength, and measured quantity, and blocks verification when a field differs.
S128: Pharmacy Verification Station uses the review slip to record the exception category, evidence checked, disposition, and reviewer identity.
S129: The Clinical Pharmacist assesses dose, route, timing, and patient-specific clinical concerns before approving a correction or rejecting the order.
S130: A correction requires a valid authorized order and must not be inferred from prior dispensing history.
S131: Larkspur keeps the cabinet transaction locked and confirms that the medication has not been administered while review is pending.
S132: The Registered Nurse escalates an urgent patient-care concern to the Clinical Pharmacist and follows the hospital's clinical response procedure.
S133: The Registered Nurse does not bypass a hold or substitute a product to clear an exception.
S134: The Charge Nurse assigns unresolved exceptions to a named role and confirms that ownership is maintained at shift handover.
S135: The Pharmacy Technician may gather package and transaction evidence but may not make a clinical dose decision.
S136: The Medication Order Gateway rejects incomplete or internally inconsistent order updates and retains the rejection reason for review.
S137: The North Ward Cabinet Controller prevents access to a held transaction until an authorized disposition is recorded.
S138: The South Ward Cabinet Controller reports a failed lock or an unrecognized access attempt for immediate operational review.
S139: The Sensor-monitored Medication Cooler reports excursions that could affect medication suitability, and affected stock remains unavailable pending assessment.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
